name: coated_sensor_oscillating
title: Coated temperature sensor in an oscillating ambient
summary: Lumped spherical sensor with a coating (spherical-shell conduction resistance in series with convection) in a sinusoidally oscillating ambient: analytical first-order response gives the sensor temperature at a given time, with Biot number, capacitance and time constant.

origin.course: Nellis & Klein, Heat Transfer (Cambridge University Press, 2009), example 3.1-2
origin.notes: Example 3.1-2 of Nellis & Klein, Heat Transfer, from the EES example set of F-Chart Software (plain-text MIT mirror: EES-Community/ees-examples, uncategorized/example_3.1-2_temperature_sensor.ees).

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solution of the original .eez (single solve at t = 10 s) using compare_solution.py --ees-units: 24 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); at rtol=1e-12 the largest relative difference is 3.35e-09 (on T_infinity). The stored time t = 10 s is the model evaluation time, so no closed-form hand check was needed.
verification.reference: EES stored solution (ees_variables.csv) of example 3.1-2 temperature sensor.eez, Nellis & Klein Heat Transfer example 3.1-2
verification.notes: Only in EES reference: T_C, T_infinity_C (dropped °C aliases of Temp/T_infinity, values equal). Only in CoolSolve: the built-in pi.
